# Method-Selection Decision Guide {#sec-method-selection-guide}

## Work backwards from the primary objective

| Design / objective | Outcome or target | Starting chapter | Calculator status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Estimate one population proportion | Binary, percentage or prevalence | @sec-single-proportion | Supported with stated approximations |
| Estimate a population mean | Continuous | @sec-single-mean | Supported with stated approximations |
| Compare two independent proportions | Binary, two groups | @sec-two-proportions | Supported for documented objectives |
| Compare two independent means | Continuous, two groups | @sec-two-means | Supported under documented normal approximations |
| Non-inferiority / equivalence | Two independent groups with prespecified margin | @sec-non-inferiority-trials / @sec-equivalence-trials | Supported for documented two-group methods |
| Estimate / test Pearson correlation | Paired measurements on independent people | @sec-correlation | Approximate Fisher-z module |
| Estimate diagnostic Se or Sp | Diseased / non-diseased strata | @sec-sensitivity-specificity | Wilson/Wald approximate modules |
| Estimate or compare ROC AUC | Diseased / non-diseased groups | @sec-auc-planning | Hanley–McNeil approximate modules |
| Cluster-randomised trial | Randomisation at cluster level | @sec-cluster-size | **Not a complete supported calculation** |
| Paired mean / repeated measures | Correlated longitudinal or paired outcomes | @sec-method-selection | **Not currently supported** |
| Time-to-event trial | Survival / hazard | @sec-method-selection | **Not currently supported** |
| Clinical prediction model development | Calibration, shrinkage, outcome events | @sec-method-selection | **Not currently supported**; use design-specific guidance [@riley2020] |

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
A design that is not supported must not be forced through the closest-looking formula. Consultation or a specialised validated method is necessary.
:::

## Ten-question pre-calculation checklist

1. What population and clinical question are being studied?
2. What is the primary outcome and measurement time?
3. Which estimand is of interest?
4. Is the goal precision or hypothesis testing?
5. Are observations independent, paired, repeated or clustered?
6. Is there a defensible target effect or precision requirement?
7. Where do planning values and uncertainty ranges come from?
8. What allocation, design, finite-population and recruitment assumptions apply?
9. Which analytic test or confidence-interval procedure is anticipated?
10. Can the calculation be replicated and its limitations reported?
